| C-01 | crypto | LEMMA | partial | Encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. | server.put() stores seal(MASTER_KEY, value), which encrypts with AESGCM under a key from AESGCM.generate_key(bit_length=256) | `vaultlite/vaultlite/crypto.py#AESGCM.generate_key(bit_length=256)`<br>`vaultlite/vaultlite/server.py#STORE[name] = seal(MASTER_KEY`<br>`vaultlite/tests/test_crypto.py`<br>`vaultlite/tests/test_audit.py` | There is no 'at rest': STORE is an in-memory dict and nothing is written to disk. Nothing checks that a loaded key is 32 bytes, so a 16-byte key would silently give AES-128. No test asserts that stored values are ciphertext. |
| C-02 | crypto | LEMMA | enforced | Every secret has its own random nonce. | seal() draws a fresh 12-byte nonce from os.urandom on every call and prefixes it to the ciphertext | `vaultlite/vaultlite/crypto.py#nonce = os.urandom(12)`<br>`vaultlite/tests/test_crypto.py` | — |
| C-03 | server | LEMMA | absent | Zero-knowledge server: the server never sees plaintext secrets. | — | — | The code contradicts the claim: server.py holds MASTER_KEY, put() receives the plaintext value and get() decrypts with open_sealed() and returns plaintext. Zero knowledge needs client-side encryption with keys the server never holds. |
| C-04 | keys | LEMMA | absent | Automatic key rotation every 30 days. | — | — | No rotation code, scheduler, key versioning or re-encryption path exists; there is a single MASTER_KEY. The only 'rotation' in the code is the constant string printed by cli.status(). |
| C-05 | audit | LEMMA | partial | Full audit log of every read, write and delete. | server.put() and server.get() call audit.log(), which appends a JSON line with time, action, name and user to audit.log | `vaultlite/vaultlite/audit.py#def log(`<br>`vaultlite/vaultlite/server.py#log("read", name, user)`<br>`vaultlite/tests/test_audit.py` | server.delete() does not call log(), so deletes are never recorded and no test covers them. The 'append-only' log is a plain file opened in append mode with no hash chain, signature or protection against editing. get() logs 'read' before the lookup, so a failed read is recorded as a read. |
